chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Postwar France: American soldiers, Marshall Plan and colonial laws
summary: Europe was changed by American influence, the Marshall Plan, price gouging, and Americans pressing bars to bar Black patrons, which French law forbade.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So now, when you were back in Europe -- that's where we started, with you going back to Europe. Then we started talking about Jean Bigard. Okay, now, what happened to you during this second trip?
Well, first, when I went back, Europe had been changed.
You're talking about rent had gone up,

Oh, everything gone up, was higher. And see, American influence was there. The American soldier, he had made Frenchmen angry with everything American. The French, he had to close up all his bordellos, which he loved. They didn't close them up. And he was -- so he decided to bait the American, and rob him, too.

So they had the Marshall Plan, and he was getting as much money as he could. And then he was robbing them, too. Everything, charged double prices for everything, triple the prices. And then, what they're doing (inaudible) trying to treat this Frenchman how to treat his black population. And in France, you had all this colonial population, man, the African population, North African and non-African.

So they was trying to tell France what to do with them, put them in their places. And they had certain little bars that they had told the managers, we'll pay you this much but don't you allow no black man to be coming in, having no drinks. Well, that is against the law and you can use your license immediately and you've got to do six months in jail.

That is the law. That is the law. If you speak derogatory about a person of color and he takes you up, you're going to get arrested on the spot. And the French policemen were angry because the American soldiers
were doing acts of and they couldn't arrest them. And they were getting angrier and angrier. 'You can't touch me.' And they'd slap the women. 'You can't touch me.'
